header.running_head: The Practices of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) with Food and Drink

blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ liked the foreleg of an animal. When the foreleg was once poisoned, everyone suspected that it was the Jews who poisoned it." [^1]

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ came to visit them in their house, they slaughtered a goat in his honour. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "It seems like they knew we like meat." There is a more detailed story attached to this incident. [^2]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ loved bottle gourd[^3] so when some food was served, I started searching for it (in the plate) and placing them in front of him because I knew that he loved it." [^4]
Hadhrat Anas (RA) also narrates that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ ate food, he licked his three fingers (with which he ate). [^5]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ (was so humble that he) ate on the floor, tied the feet of goats when they were to be milked and even accepted the invitation of slaves to eat (plain) barley bread." [^6]
Hadhrat Yahyaa bin Abu Katheer reports that a plate of Thareed came to Rasulullaah ﷺ every day from Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA). It went with him to the house of whichever wife he was with. [^7]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when some goat's milk was milked for Rasulullaah ﷺ, he drank it and then gargled his mouth saying, "It has some stickiness (which needs to be rinsed out to preserve oral hygiene)." [^8]

Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once stopped over at a certain place, a woman sent her son with a goat to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ milked the goat and told the boy to take it to his mother. After she had drunk to her fill, the boy brought another goat. After milking it, Rasulullaah ﷺ gave the milk to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). When the boy then brought a third goat, Rasulullaah ﷺ milked it and only this time did he drink. [^9]

Hadhrat Ibraheem (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to keep his right hand free for acts such as eating, drinking and making wudhu. His left hand he would keep free for acts such as Istinjaa, cleaning his nose and other such acts. [^10]
